Hex voice dictation on Omarchy

Hex is local-first voice dictation by Anomaly (the new Rust rewrite of Kit Langton's dictation app): hold a key, speak, release, and Hex transcribes on your machine with a local speech model and pastes the text into whatever app you're in. The Linux build is a beta that covers x86_64/ARM64, X11, and wlroots Wayland compositors like Omarchy's Hyprland.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add hex-bin

Install Hex on Omarchy with one command. 21.8 MB download, 57 MB installed, version 3.0.0-1. Launch it from the app launcher or hex in a terminal. First launch downloads a speech model (the app needs huggingface.co reachable for that) — after that, dictation runs fully on-device. Start Hex at login with systemctl --user enable hex.service. MIT-licensed, free, no account.

Not the hex-dump tool: Arch's hex package installs /usr/bin/hx. This package is hex-bin, the dictation app, and installs /usr/bin/hex — they don't conflict.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. First launch.

Open Hex from the launcher (or run hex). It opens a 980×760 window with Settings, Modes, and History. The first thing it does is download a speech model for on-device transcription — pick a language and model (English + Parakeet is a good default), then let it finish. Per the docs, Hex is one process per user: closing the window doesn't stop dictation or a model download; quit from the tray menu or with hex quit.

2. The 3 things you need to know:

  • The shortcut does nothing on Omarchy until you bind it. Hyprland accepts the GlobalShortcuts portal but delivers nothing unless you bind the key yourself — the key you record in Hex's Settings is ignored. Add this to your Hyprland config (prefer keys without modifiers; modifiers can leak into the paste keystroke): 
    bind = , End, global, hex:dictation
bind = F9, global, hex:paste-last
    Then: press End, speak, press End again (Toggle mode) — or bind hex dictation start / hex dictation stop to key press/release for hold-to-dictate. Double-press the key to keep recording; press again to finish. Option-Shift-V (or hex paste-last) re-pastes the last dictation.
  • Everything is paste, not typing. Hex copies the transcript, then pastes with Ctrl+V through wtype (wlroots compositors) or the desktop's RemoteDesktop portal. If paste fails, the transcript stays on your clipboard with "Copied to the clipboard; press Ctrl+V to paste" — see the fixes below.
  • The tray runs the show. When the desktop has a StatusNotifierItem host (Omarchy's bar qualifies), Hex shows a tray icon: click to open the window, or use the menu — Show Hex, Paste last dictation, model list, update (Restart to update), Enable / Disable Hex, Quit Hex. While recording or transcribing, the menu and tooltip say so.

3. Config location.

App settings live in settings.json in Hex's data directory (run hex logs to find the path — unverified on Omarchy). Power-user transforms go in ~/.config/hex/hex.config.ts (TypeScript/JavaScript, reloaded on save; no filesystem/network/process access). Launch-at-login is systemctl --user enable hex.service; the docs also suggest this Hyprland line so the service inherits your session display:

exec-once = dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP

Common issues & fixes

All sourced from the project's docs and issue tracker. Nothing below was reproduced on Omarchy — confirm each fix on-machine before relying on it.

Pressing the shortcut does nothing on Omarchy

Expected — Hyprland "takes every shortcut without a key," so Hex can't bind anything itself (docs/linux.md).

Fix: Bind it in ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf: bind = , End, global, hex:dictation for toggle, or press/release binds of hex dictation start / hex dictation stop for hold-to-dictate. If it still does nothing, confirm Hex is running (hex status) — the hex control commands never start it, they only talk to the running process.

Dictation finishes but nothing pastes ("Copied to the clipboard")

Per the docs, this happens when neither paste path is available: on Hyprland you need wl-clipboard and wtype installed (they're optdepends of the package).

Fix: Install them: sudo pacman -S --needed wl-clipboard wtype. The first paste on some desktops asks you to approve keyboard control via the RemoteDesktop portal; approve it once and Hex keeps the restore token. (docs/linux.md: Native Wayland Requirements)

The pasted text arrives wrong

Documented Wayland behavior: Hex can't see held keys, and Hyprland merges still-held modifiers into the paste keystroke — e.g. you held Alt+Z and the paste became Ctrl+Alt+V. Hex waits for the shortcut's release plus 250 ms before pasting (fixed path for issue #354).

Fix: Release the modifiers before the transcript arrives, or bind modifier-less keys (End, F-keys). A modifier held past ~2 s still changes the paste.

The recording HUD/overlay never appears on Omarchy

Known open issue: issue #756 — on pure Wayland without layer-shell support for Hex's overlay, the HUD is unavailable. Also see issue #814 — the Hex window maps too small on Linux/Wayland (the app is meant to auto-float at 980×760). Both open as of 2026-11-01.

Fix: The window itself and dictation still work; use the tray icon's recording indicator instead. Monitor both issues before claiming anything is fixed.

Hex quits immediately on launch, or says your processor is unsupported

Two separate causes from the docs: x86_64 builds require a 2013-or-newer CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Excavator or later) — the app shows a message and quits otherwise. Separately, even with CPU inference the window needs a Vulkan driver; vulkan-icd-loader alone isn't a driver.

Fix: Install your GPU's Vulkan driver or a software one (mesa provides lavapipe) before reporting a black/blank window.

First-run model download fails on a restricted network

App downloads come from anoma.ly, but model setup needs huggingface.co and its model CDN — a successful app download doesn't prove those are reachable (docs).

Fix: Allow both hosts, then retry model preparation in Settings › Transcription Model. Diagnostic view: hex logs -n 40 or journalctl --user -u hex.service.

Pairs well with / If you hate this, try

Pairs well with

  • omawrite (dictate your draft, edit it in a real writing app)
  • omarchy-meeting-recorder-bin (capture the audio for meetings, Hex-style)
  • wl-clipboard (the clipboard backend Hex pastes through)

If you hate this, try

  • Nerd Dictation — free, open-source Linux dictation built on Vosk (yay -S nerd-dictation-git; needs a vosk-model) — fully offline, but raw word accuracy is a step below Hex's models and there's no app like Hex's window/tray.

Verdict: If you want Superwhisper-style "hold a key and talk" dictation on an Omarchy box without paying or sending audio to a cloud, Hex is the only serious option; Nerd Dictation is the fallback if you insist on zero setup UI.

Hex is a free alternative to Superwhisper ($8.33/mo) and Wispr Flow ($20/mo)

Hex is a free alternative to Superwhisper ($8.33/mo) and Wispr Flow ($20/mo) — on Linux, where neither runs. What you give up: their LLM rewrite/polish passes on every dictation (Hex has optional Modes text processing, plus optional OpenCode post-processing if you run OpenCode — not the same as a built-in AI editor), and meeting transcription (macOS-only in Hex). What you keep: the core loop — hold a key, speak, get pasted text anywhere — with on-device transcription, so your audio never leaves the machine. Free and MIT-licensed.

How to switch from commercial dictation

No migration needed: commercial dictation tools keep no exportable state worth migrating — your habit transfers, nothing else. Install Hex, bind the shortcut in your Hyprland config, install wl-clipboard + wtype, and the core loop (hold a key, speak, get text) works the same from day one. What you leave behind: per-dictation LLM polish (Superwhisper/Wispr Flow) and meeting transcription (macOS-only anyway). What you gain: no subscription, no cloud, and dictation inside any Omarchy app — not just the browser.

Frequently asked questions

Does Hex work on Omarchy?

Yes — the Linux beta targets exactly this stack: wlroots Wayland compositors including Hyprland. Install with omarchy pkg add hex-bin, bind the shortcut in your Hyprland config (the in-app shortcut recorder is ignored on Hyprland), and install wl-clipboard + wtype so pasting works.

Is Hex free?

Yes. MIT-licensed open source by Anomaly (anomalyco/hex). Ordinary dictation needs no account and no cloud service; the store listing says to check the project site for current pricing, so confirm before treating this as permanent.

Does dictation work offline?

Yes, after the one-time model download — transcription runs on-device (Vulkan GPU when available, CPU fallback). No audio is saved by default, and history keeps only pasted text for 7 days (configurable, can be turned off).

Is this the same as the hex hex-dump tool?

No. The Arch package hex is a hex viewer (installs /usr/bin/hx). hex-bin is the dictation app (installs /usr/bin/hex). The PKGBUILD explicitly documents this distinction; they don't conflict.

Can I cancel a dictation?

No — Escape never cancels; every dictation finishes and pastes (documented behavior; see the discussion in issue #786). To drop one, finish it and delete the text.

How do I uninstall it cleanly?

omarchy pkg drop hex-bin, then systemctl --user disable --now hex.service if you enabled it, and remove the data directory (hex logs shows the path; model downloads live there — unverified, confirm during the verify pass).
